label: conj:reidemeister-mass-invariance
title: Reidemeister invariance of mass and binding energy
html:
Conjecture (conditional on conj:borromean-quark). The topological mass formula is a knot invariant (R-I, R-II, R-III). The binding energy of linked particles is an embedding invariant (R-II, R-III but not R-I). Shell transitions are R-I moves on the embedding. (The three Reidemeister invariances follow from the hyperbolic-volume invariant and the embedding structure; the shell-transition R-I reading is the conjectural part.)

The three Reidemeister moves.

Every deformation of a knot diagram decomposes into a sequence of three local moves:

  • R-I (curl): add or remove a single crossing (writhe changes by \pm 1).
  • R-II (poke): add or remove a pair of crossings with opposite signs (writhe unchanged).
  • R-III (slide): move a strand past a crossing (crossing number unchanged).

Topological mass: invariant under all three.

The bare mass of a particle is determined by the hyperbolic volume of its knot complement and the per-block density:

  m_{\mathrm{bare}}(K) = 
  m_e \cdot \frac{\mathrm{Vol}(S^3 \setminus K) \, \rho(K)}{\hbar_q^2}.

The hyperbolic volume is a topological invariant of the knot type — it does not depend on the diagram — and the per-block density \rho(K) is computed from the Markov trace of the braid closure, itself a knot invariant. Since Reidemeister's theorem states that two diagrams represent the same knot if and only if they are related by a finite sequence of R-I, R-II, R-III moves:

  m_{\mathrm{bare}}
   \text{is invariant under R-I, R-II, R-III.}

The electron mass \mathfrak{m}_e \approx 0.511 MeV (from vacuum drag, since \mathrm{Vol}(T_{2,3}) = 0) does not change when the electron is excited. The proton mass \mathfrak{m}_{\mathfrak{p}} \approx 938 MeV (from \mathrm{Vol}(\mathcal{B}_3)) does not change when the atom is ionised. Mass is a property of the knot type, not the diagram.

Binding energy: invariant under R-II and R-III only.

The binding energy of a linked pair (electron--proton, or nucleon--nucleon) is the crossing energy of the Hopf link connecting them:

  \mathfrak{E}_{\mathrm{bind}}
  = 
  \sum_{\text{crossings of link}}
  \epsilon_i \cdot q^{\pm 1}

where the sum runs over the crossings of the embedding of one particle's knot inside the other's Seifert surface.

  • R-III (strand slide): rearranges crossings without changing their number or signs. The crossing energy sum is invariant. \checkmark

  • R-II (poke): adds two crossings of opposite sign. Their contributions to the crossing energy are +q \cdot \epsilon and -q^{-1} \cdot \epsilon. In the Skein resolution, the pair resolves to (q - q^{-1}) \cdot \epsilon \cdot L_0, where L_0 is the smoothed state. For a virtual pair (the two crossings are adjacent), L_0 is the original link and the contributions cancel to leading order. The binding energy is invariant. \checkmark

  • R-I (curl): adds a single crossing. This changes the writhe by \pm 1 and adds a crossing energy contribution \pm q^{\pm 1} \cdot \epsilon that does not cancel. The binding energy changes. \times

  \mathfrak{E}_{\mathrm{bind}}
   \text{is invariant under R-II, R-III but \textbf{not} R-I.}

Shell transitions are R-I moves.

When a photon is absorbed by the hydrogen atom, the electron trefoil T_{2,3} undergoes a Reidemeister I move within its Hopf link to the proton: a curl is added to the trefoil diagram at the exceptional divisor. The writhe changes from w to w + 2 (a pair of R-I moves adding two curls to preserve the knot type's minimal crossing structure):

  n \to n + 1
  \qquad\Longleftrightarrow\qquad
  w \to w + 2
  \qquad\Longleftrightarrow\qquad
  \text{two R-I moves on the embedding.}

The bare mass \mathfrak{m}_e is unchanged (R-I is a knot invariant). The binding energy E_n = -13.6/n^2 eV changes (R-I is NOT an embedding invariant). The difference \Delta E = E_{n+1} - E_n is the photon energy.

Summary.

Quantity R-I R-II R-III Physical meaning
Bare mass \checkmark \checkmark \checkmark Particle identity (knot type)
Binding energy \times \checkmark \checkmark Bound state energy (embedding)
Shell number n \times \checkmark \checkmark Writhe level of embedding
Knot type \checkmark \checkmark \checkmark Which particle it is
Writhe w \times \checkmark \times^* Diagram-dependent

{}^*R-III preserves writhe but is not the only invariance of writhe; writhe is a regular isotopy invariant (R-II + R-III), not a knot invariant (R-I + R-II + R-III).

Physical consequence.

A particle's identity (which knot type: electron, muon, proton, neutron) is determined by R-I + R-II + R-III invariants — the topological knot type. A particle's state (which shell, which orbital) is determined by R-II + R-III invariants — the regular isotopy class of the embedding. The difference between identity and state is precisely one Reidemeister move: R-I.

This is why an excited hydrogen atom is still hydrogen: the electron is still a trefoil (knot type unchanged by R-I). But it is in a different state: the trefoil's writhe is different (embedding changed by R-I), and the binding energy differs.

Archimedean specialisation. What follows sits on the archimedean side of the substrate wall: it invokes real- or complex-analytic constructs — real-valued physical observables, real-analytic bounds, transcendental constants, or numerical evaluation at the substrate parameter q_0. Any generic categorical / q-deformation identities it draws on remain valid over an abstract coefficient ring; only their archimedean realisation is specialised here.
